_comment: The byte-identity pin for `POST /api/skills/run` request bodies (#538).
Three languages read this one file and assert their builder emits `expected`
byte for byte: Rust in `client/core/tests/skills_run_bodies.rs`, TypeScript in
suite (a JVM test cannot call uniffi, so the JVM side pins only that the lane
sends the core's string verbatim). `expected` is the real wire text: the web
posts exactly `JSON.stringify(body)` and the Kotlin client posts the core's
string unchanged, so key ORDER is part of the contract, not formatting.
Add a case here rather than to any one language's own suite — a case that
exists in one place proves nothing about the other two.

cases.name: microtask: a bare run sends nothing but the ref
microtask: replace false is omitted, not sent as a literal false
microtask: grain rides along, replace absent
microtask: every arg set, in declaration order
microtask: an empty model omits the key entirely
grill-me: an interview opens with an empty turns array
grill-me: one completed round threads back question and answer
grill-me: the whole conversation, never a trimmed subset
cases.expected: {"skill":"grill-me","args":{"ref":"i","turns":[{"question":{"prompt":"Which airport?","recommendedAnswer":"SEA","choices":["SEA","PDX"]},"answer":"SEA"},{"question":{"prompt":"Which dates?","recommendedAnswer":"next week","choices":["next week","in a month","not decided"]},"answer":"the third week of September"}]}}

cases.name: grill-me: an answer with characters JSON must escape

question.prompt: Say it in your own words

cases.expected: {"skill":"grill-me","args":{"ref":"i","turns":[{"question":{"prompt":"Say it in your own words","recommendedAnswer":"anything","choices":["a","b"]},"answer":"he said \"soon\"\nand left"}]}}
